## What's fixed

- **Music that goes quiet in the background comes back by itself.** iOS keeps an app running in the background only while it makes sound, and something could still silence Kultr mid-song: iOS stopping the player, or a stream that stalled without failing. Kultr waited, and after half a minute of quiet iOS suspended it, so the music stopped until you pressed play. Now, when Kultr should be playing but has been silent for four seconds, it tells the player to play again. If that doesn't work by twelve seconds, it reloads the song where it stopped. Both happen well before iOS would suspend it.
- **A stalled stream gives up sooner.** A connection that stops sending without dropping used to hang for a minute, longer than iOS lets a quiet app run. It now fails after 20 seconds, so Kultr can retry the song while it is still running.
- **Lighter in the background.** Kultr frees its cover-art memory when you leave it. Of the apps playing in the background, iOS closes the largest first when it needs memory.
- **The library check iOS runs in the background now finishes on time.** If it ran out of time, iOS could close Kultr while music was playing.

## New: Playback log

**Settings → About → Playback log** records what played, every pause and its cause (Lock Screen, headphones, a call, iOS), and what iOS did to Kultr in the background. That includes memory warnings, suspensions, crashes and the cases where iOS closed it. If the music still stops by itself, open the log, tap the share button and send it to me, so I can see exactly what happened.

## Install

Download **Kultr.ipa** below and install it with **Sideloadly** (Windows, Mac), **AltStore** (Windows, Mac) or **Impactor** (Linux) — or with no computer at all, through **SideStore** installed by **SideInstaller** (only from sideinstaller.net) with **LocalDevVPN** connected. Or add the source `https://gist.githubusercontent.com/evropiani/6e3a3c18525a228d03924674430c4d48/raw/evropiani.json` in SideStore and update from there.

Installing over an earlier version keeps your servers, library, listening history, analysis and downloads — install it with the same Apple ID and don't delete the old app first.
